summary: Intro call to map Solanum's security and hosting constraints for LLM inference. Primary concerns: BYOK/KMS + HSM, SSO/SAML via Okta, RBAC for model access, audit log retention and e-discovery, SOC2 evidence and ISO interest, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private fits their regulatory needs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We also have Priya, our solutions engineer. Could you do quick intros?
[00:07] Dr. Mia Alvarez: Hi, I'm Mia, CTO at Solanum. We're building internal assistive tools for bench scientists—sensitive PII-ish, and IP.
[00:14] Ethan Cole: Ethan here, head of infra. We'll be responsible for networking and any private deployment.
[00:18] Lena Park: Lena, security engineer. I'll be asking the hard questions about keys and logs.
[00:22] Priya Patel: Hi all, Priya — I'll cover architecture and deployment options.
[00:27] Jordan Lee: Great. High level, we want to understand compliance posture and gating criteria for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. What are your must-haves?
[00:33] Dr. Mia Alvarez: SOC 2 Type II is mandatory, and we have a stretch ask for ISO 27001. Also, we need BYOK for anything with customer data; we can't have keys that Redwood manages for certain datasets.
[00:43] Lena Park: Right — BYOK + HSM backed keys. We also need strong RBAC: separate environments for research vs production models, audit trails for model prompts and responses for at least 12 months, and the ability to export logs for e-discovery.
[00:56] Priya Patel: Understood. Quick clarification: when you say export logs, do you mean full token-level logs or redacted summaries?
[01:02] Lena Park: Preferably full request/response metadata with the option to redact content. We have legal requests occasionally that require full context.
[01:09] Jordan Lee: Cool. On SOC2, Redwood is SOC2 Type II — we can share the report and the last penetration test exec summary. Hosted customers often use our managed KMS, but for BYOK we offer an integration where customers bring keys via their KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) and we support HSM-backed key wraps.
[01:26] Ethan Cole: So for BYOK, are keys ever in Redwood's control? We need to know if key material leaves our account.
[01:31] Priya Patel: Key material never leaves the customer's KMS in the BYOK flow. We exchange wrapped keys and perform envelope encryption. For on-prem/private deployments you can provision an HSM in your VPC — that gives you full control.
[01:41] Dr. Mia Alvarez: Ok that helps. What about SSO — we use Okta and SAML. We need SCIM provisioning and role sync to map our teams.
[01:48] Jordan Lee: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is configurable with role bindings, and we have audit logs tied to token-level usage per-API key.
[01:55] Lena Park: Is RBAC enforced at the model route level? We can't have research folks hitting production fine-tuned models.
[02:01] Priya Patel: Yes, routes and model versions can be scoped to teams. You can create model-level roles: read, invoke, manage. Policies can be enforced via our Private control plane when you're on Dedicated or Private. Hosted supports role mappings too but for strict isolation Dedicated or Private is better.
[02:11] Ethan Cole: Latency tradeoffs? We have throughput spikes during batch jobs but need low latency for interactive scientist tooling.
[02:18] Priya Patel: Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable latency and autoscaling policies. Hosted can work for many cases but might involve routing to multiple model variants; caching reduces cost but could affect cold-start paths. Private in your VPC gives the most control but requires ops overhead.
[02:30] Dr. Mia Alvarez: On the logs retention, you said token-level logs. Is there a way to configure retention per project?
[02:36] Jordan Lee: Yes, retention is configurable by route/project. Hosted defaults to 90 days for raw transcripts unless you opt into extended retention. Enterprise customers can extend to 12 months or longer with additional contract terms. You can also push logs to your cloud storage for long-term retention.
[02:49] Lena Park: We need immutable audit trails for 7 years for certain clinical projects. Is log export automated?
[02:55] Priya Patel: You can stream audit logs in real time to your account (CloudWatch, Stackdriver, or S3/GCS buckets). For immutability you can land them to an append-only store or a WORM bucket in your cloud account.
[03:06] Ethan Cole: What about encryption in transit and at rest?
[03:09] Jordan Lee: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. If you use BYOK, the data keys are wrapped with your KMS CMK. For Private we also support network-level isolation — VPC peering, private endpoints.
[03:20] Lena Park: Auditors always ask for separation of duties. Who has access to customer logs on Redwood side?
[03:25] Priya Patel: Access is strictly role-based and logged; SRE/ops access to customer data requires a documented process and is approved via change control. We can provide an access matrix and recent audit evidence.
[03:33] Dr. Mia Alvarez: Do you retain model prompts/responses for embeddings use cases? That could be sensitive.
[03:38] Jordan Lee: Embeddings generation can be configured to not persist raw inputs or to persist only hashed tokens for similarity use. We offer opt-out flags or automatic redaction for PII detection.
[03:47] Lena Park: About SOC2 evidence — we need the control mappings for encryption, access control, incident response. Can you provide a control matrix?
[03:53] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll send a control mapping doc that maps Redwood controls to SOC2 criteria, and a ticked crosswalk for ISO 27001 if you want to evaluate that.
[04:01] Ethan Cole: Network-level: if we choose Private, can we run everything behind our firewall? We need air-gapped options for a subset of workloads.
[04:07] Priya Patel: We have an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments — it's heavier lift but feasible. For VPC-hosted Private deployments, we do a customer-managed control plane so your traffic never traverses public internet — that's often a good middle ground.
[04:18] Dr. Mia Alvarez: Do you offer long-term retention for logs in case of legal holds?
[04:22] Jordan Lee: Yes, via log export to your storage; retention can be enforced via your bucket policies. We can also support archival to cold storage with retrieval SLAs.
[04:30] Lena Park: Are there certifications for the infrastructure providers you use? Some of our legal team asks about the cloud providers' compliance posture.
[04:36] Priya Patel: We publish our third-party provider list and their certifications (AWS, GCP) — summarized in the security pack.
[04:41] Ethan Cole: What about data residency — some of our EU customers require data never leave EU.
[04:45] Jordan Lee: We support region-restricted deployments and routing. Hosted can be pinned to a region where we operate. Dedicated and Private obviously run in the region you select and you can ensure no cross-region replication.
[04:55] Dr. Mia Alvarez: Can we run a PoC where we test dedicated instance for a week and push a small workload?
[04:59] Priya Patel: Absolutely — we typically do a smoke PoC: provision a small dedicated pool, run a benchmark harness against your typical prompts, and capture latency/cost metrics.
[05:07] Lena Park: About SSO again — can we auto-provision service accounts for CI pipelines and have machine identities?
[05:12] Jordan Lee: Yes, there are service principals and API keys scoped to roles. We recommend short-lived tokens and renewal via your identity provider where possible.
[05:19] Ethan Cole: One more — audit log tampering. How do you guarantee logs weren't altered?
[05:24] Priya Patel: For high-integrity logs we recommend streaming to your WORM storage, and we can sign logs with a server-side keychain for verifiability.
[05:33] Dr. Mia Alvarez: Any common pitfalls customers hit switching from Hosted to Dedicated?
[05:37] Priya Patel: Mostly around HA and scaling policies — Dedicated gives predictability but you need to plan autoscaling and burst rules. Also model updates are controlled by rollouts so CI integration is important.
[05:48] Lena Park: For forensic reviews, do you provide request/response hashes to prove content integrity?
[05:52] Jordan Lee: We can provide hashed evidence and chain-of-custody logs showing who exported what and when.
[05:58] Ethan Cole: Ok, timeline — we need to be live with an internal-only prototype in Q3. Our procurement window is tight.
[06:04] Jordan Lee: Makes sense — we'll prioritize getting you SOC2 docs and the dedicated cost spreadsheet this week. Also propose a PoC the week of 2025-06-30.
[06:13] Dr. Mia Alvarez: Sounds good. Anything else on regulatory — HIPAA? Some datasets will be PHI.
[06:18] Priya Patel: Redwood provides a BAA for customers handling PHI; we have controls for handling PHI and data separation. We'll flag that as a must-have in the follow-up.
[06:26] Lena Park: Keep in mind we may require annual penetration test results and staff background checks for anyone with access to our infra.
[06:32] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll include our recent pentest summary and access control policy.
[06:36] Ethan Cole: Is there any sandbox for us to test SCIM mappings before full provisioning?
[06:40] Priya Patel: Yes, we have a staging tenant where you can run SCIM/SSO flows and test role mappings. We'll open access for Lena.
[06:47] Dr. Mia Alvarez: Ok great. Recap please?
[06:50] Jordan Lee: Recap: 1) Redwood to send SOC2 Type II report, pentest summary, control matrix, and third-party provider list; 2) Priya to share dedicated vs hosted perf/cost spreadsheet and PoC plan; 3) Schedule PoC smoke test week of 2025-06-30; 4) Lena to share Solanum's retention and PHI scope.
[07:10] Lena Park: I'll email retention scope and HIPAA notes.
[07:14] Jordan Lee: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and docs. Appreciate your time.
[07:20] Dr. Mia Alvarez: Thanks.
[07:22] [call ends]
